title: From Army Cadets in India to Canadian Champion: Avtar Nanrey Makes Rifle Shooting History
excerpt: Indian-origin marksman Avtar Nanrey, a software architect from Brampton, Ontario, has become the first person of Indian descent to win a national rifle shooting championship in Canada, capping a remarkable return to competitive shooting after a 14-year hiatus.
body:
• Indian-origin marksman Avtar Nanrey won a double national championship at the DCRA Canadian Championships, making history as a person of Indian descent in Canadian rifle shooting.
  • Nanrey, a software architect at IBM Canada based in Brampton, Ontario, began shooting with the Army Cadets in India in 2005 before a 14-year break from the sport.
  • Since returning to competitive shooting in 2022, Nanrey has risen rapidly through the ranks, representing Canada at Bisley and leading Team Canada to an aggregate title at the 2026 Southwest Nationals.
  • His achievements span both domestic and international competition, including the 2026 NRA National High Power Long-Range Championship in the United States.

Avtar Nanrey, an Indian-origin software architect based in Brampton, Ontario, has written himself into Canadian rifle shooting history with a double national championship victory at the Dominion of Canada Rifle Association's annual championships, held at the Connaught Ranges in Ottawa.

The achievement is all the more remarkable given Nanrey's unconventional path to the top of Canadian marksmanship. His shooting career began not in Canada but in India, where he won the Army Cadets Championship in his very first competition in 2005. After immigrating to Canada, a 14-year hiatus from competitive shooting followed — from 2007 to 2021 — before Nanrey picked up a rifle again.

A Rapid Rise Through the Ranks

When Nanrey resumed competitive shooting in 2022 with the support of the Ontario Rifle Association, his talent quickly became apparent. In his first year back, he won nearly every match in the Expert classification. By 2023, he had moved up to dominate the Master's class, securing second place in the Lieutenant Governor's match and the Grand Aggregate — two of the most prestigious individual prizes in Canadian fullbore rifle shooting.

His progression continued in 2024 when he was selected for the Canadian Rifle Team to compete at the 155th Imperial Meeting at Bisley, the spiritual home of long-range rifle shooting in England. He also represented Canada on the Palma Team that traveled to South Africa.

2026: A Breakout Year

Nanrey's 2026 season has been exceptional across multiple continents. At the Berger Southwest Nationals in Arizona, he finished second overall in the mid-range aggregate with a score of 599-40X at 600 yards and placed third in the Sling division of the Palma match at 800, 900, and 1,000 yards with 448-24X.

He then led Team Canada to the Team Aggregate title at the Southwest Nationals with a personal score of 649-45X, the highest on the squad coached by Peter Westlake.

At the NRA National High Power Long-Range Championship in Malvern, Ohio, Nanrey was part of the USNRT-Gill team that won the Cowboy Team Trophy in the Palma Team Championship. He also featured among leading individual scores at the DCRA Canadian Championships, recording 295.32 in the America Match against Great Britain and the United States.

Beyond the Range

Away from competition, Nanrey works as a software architect at IBM Canada and is a father of two. The Ontario Rifle Association has celebrated his achievements as a proud moment for Canadian marksmanship, noting that both he and fellow Ontario shooter Fazal Mohideen dominated the Palma and Sling rifle categories at the 2026 Southwest Nationals.

His journey — from Army Cadets in India to the pinnacle of Canadian rifle shooting — mirrors the broader story of Indian-origin athletes making their mark in adopted countries across disciplines that receive little mainstream attention but demand extraordinary precision and dedication.
nri_angle: An Indian-origin immigrant who began shooting with Army Cadets in India makes history at the top of Canadian rifle marksmanship.
